title: Plinth, Plutus Tx, and Untyped Plutus Core
section: Plinth, Plutus Tx, and Untyped Plutus Core
topics: Plinth, Plutus Tx, and Untyped Plutus Core
text: Plinth is the current name for the Haskell-based language formerly called Plutus Tx. It expresses validator logic and compiles to Untyped Plutus Core, or UPLC. UPLC, rather than ordinary Haskell source, is interpreted when nodes validate a transaction. Other high-level languages can also compile to UPLC. Typed Plutus Core and Plutus IR are compiler intermediate representations; they should not be confused with the on-chain UPLC language. Learning Haskell is useful for Plinth, but not every Haskell program is a valid Plinth validator.
version_scope: See the cited source; no automatic version compatibility is assumed.

title: Ledger, protocol, Plutus Core, and package versions
section: Ledger, protocol, Plutus Core, and package versions
topics: Ledger, protocol, Plutus Core, and package versions
text: Distinguish ledger language version, Plutus Core language version, protocol version, builtin semantics, and Haskell package version. Ledger tags such as Plutus V1, V2 and V3 determine how scripts interact with the ledger. A package release number is not a ledger version. Plutus Core 1.1.0 introduced the case and constr syntax for sums of products. Builtin availability and behavior also depend on ledger and protocol configuration; a new builtin does not necessarily require a new Core language version. The documentation illustrates changed consByteString behavior for invalid byte values. Check the documented version combination before claiming a feature is usable on a target network.
version_scope: See the cited source; no automatic version compatibility is assumed.

title: Plutus V1, V2, V3 validator arguments and ScriptContext
section: Plutus V1, V2, V3 validator arguments and ScriptContext
topics: Plutus V1, V2, V3 validator arguments and ScriptContext
text: A validator receives transaction information through ScriptContext. Its representation and validator invocation depend on the ledger language version. A Plutus V1 or V2 spending script receives datum, redeemer and context arguments; other script purposes have different interfaces. Plutus V3 scripts take one script-context argument, with redeemer and script information carried inside that context, and successful evaluation must return the expected unit value. V3 additionally supports voting and proposing script purposes. Do not teach a three-argument validator signature as universal across V1, V2 and V3. Reference inputs and governance-related transaction fields also have version-specific compatibility constraints.
version_scope: Comparison of V1, V2, V3. Each chunk is evidence only for the version it describes.

title: Extended UTXO model explainer
text: An unspent transaction output, or UTXO, is a previous transaction output that has not been consumed. A transaction consumes whole inputs and creates new outputs, including change where needed. A particular output can be spent only once. Cardano's extended UTXO model allows spending conditions to be expressed as scripts and permits outputs to carry data. A contract can represent evolving state by spending one output and creating another with updated data. This does not mean an existing UTXO is mutated in place. Wallets construct transactions that satisfy the relevant spending rules.
version_scope: See the cited source; no automatic version compatibility is assumed.

title: Two-phase validation and collateral
text: Cardano distinguishes phase-1 transaction checks from phase-2 script execution. A phase-1 failure causes rejection before scripts run. Collateral addresses the cost of executing scripts that fail phase-2 validation; therefore, saying every failed smart-contract transaction is free is incorrect. A transaction using phase-2 scripts supplies an execution budget and collateral-related inputs. The documentation also explains collateral return: excess collateral can be returned using the relevant transaction fields instead of taking the entire amount. The exact behavior depends on whether the failure is in phase 1 or phase 2 and on the transaction's supported features.
version_scope: See the cited source; no automatic version compatibility is assumed.

title: Auction validator: parameters, datum, redeemer, state transitions
section: Auction validator: parameters, datum, redeemer, state transitions
topics: Auction validator: parameters, datum, redeemer, state transitions
text: The official auction example separates fixed contract parameters, datum, redeemer, and script context. Parameters hold configuration such as the seller or minimum bid. The datum represents the evolving highest bid. The redeemer indicates the attempted action, such as placing a bid or requesting payout. ScriptContext gives the transaction information the validator checks. A new bid must satisfy conditions including sufficient value, permitted time, refund of the previous bidder, and a continuing output with the correct datum and value. A continuing output pays to the same script address, enabling the next state transition. The example uses Plutus V3 and is explicitly educational, not a production-ready audited contract.
version_scope: Plutus V3 educational auction; explicitly not production-audited code.

title: CIP-31: Reference inputs
text: CIP-31 specifies reference inputs: transaction inputs that make an existing output available for inspection without consuming it. Spending inputs and reference inputs have different roles. Reading shared data through a reference input avoids requiring that data output to be spent and recreated merely to read it. The referenced output must still exist when the transaction is validated. The proposal describes changes to transaction structure and script context; its interface should be interpreted together with the target ledger language and protocol rules.
version_scope: Specification text; check proposal status and relevant ledger/protocol support.

title: CIP-32: Inline datums
text: CIP-32 specifies inline datums, where an output can carry the datum itself rather than only a hash referring to it. Datum hashes and inline datums are distinct representations; an explanation should state which is being used. Inline datums make the data available with the output, reducing the need to communicate a separate datum preimage off-chain. Larger stored data affects the minimum value required for the output. There are compatibility restrictions for older Plutus script versions, so an application must check its transaction and script-version combination.
version_scope: Specification text; check proposal status and relevant ledger/protocol support.

title: CIP-33: Reference scripts
text: CIP-33 specifies reference scripts. An output may store a script so a later transaction can reference that script rather than include another full copy in its witnesses. A reference script is code, while an inline datum is data; they are not interchangeable concepts. Reference inputs provide the mechanism for making the output containing a reference script available to the transaction without spending it. This can reduce repeated transaction size, but it does not eliminate the need to satisfy script validation or account for storage costs.
version_scope: Specification text; check proposal status and relevant ledger/protocol support.

title: CIP-40: Collateral output
text: CIP-40 introduces a collateral-return output and an explicit total-collateral amount. These fields allow the ledger to collect the required collateral while returning the remainder when a phase-2 script fails. Collateral return is not an ordinary successful spending output and should be explained in the context of the transaction's failure path. The proposal addresses the inconvenience of preparing collateral UTXOs with an exact value. It does not mean phase-2 validation failures are cost-free.
version_scope: Specification text; check proposal status and relevant ledger/protocol support.

title: CIP-57: Plutus Contract Blueprint
text: CIP-57 defines a machine-readable Plutus contract blueprint, commonly named plutus.json. The blueprint documents validator interfaces, including redeemer, optional datum, parameters, and optionally compiled code and hashes. It uses JSON Schema concepts plus vocabulary for Plutus data. Such metadata can support serialization tools, code generation, documentation, and wallet integration. A blueprint describes an interface; it does not prove that the validator logic is secure, and it must match the actual contract version.
version_scope: Specification text; check proposal status and relevant ledger/protocol support.

title: CIP-85: Sums of products in Plutus Core
section: CIP-85: Sums of products in Plutus Core
topics: CIP-85: Sums of products in Plutus Core
text: CIP-85 introduces sums-of-products support in Plutus Core through constructor and case terms. A constructor groups values with a tag; a case expression chooses a branch according to the constructor. This supports representations of algebraic data types without requiring all structure to be encoded indirectly with functions. Distinguish this Core syntax from the ledger's Plutus V1/V2/V3 tags and from the separate builtin Plutus Data constructors used in datum serialization.
version_scope: Specification text; check proposal status and relevant ledger/protocol support.

title: Plutus compiler and debugger CLI
text: The plutus command-line tool checks, converts, optimizes, runs, and debugs Plutus-related intermediate programs locally. It is not the same executable or interface as cardano-cli, which is used for ledger and transaction operations. The documentation distinguishes safe optimization settings from aggressive settings that may change semantics. Consult the tool's help and the version-matched guide rather than substituting commands from a different CLI. This summary is not a complete installation or command reference.
version_scope: plutus CLI, not cardano-cli; use tool-specific commands.

title: Differences between Plinth and Haskell
text: Plinth is a restricted Haskell-based language rather than unrestricted Haskell on the blockchain. The official differences guide documents supported features, representations and evaluation considerations. Code should use the appropriate Plutus libraries and compiler settings instead of assuming every Prelude operation or Haskell feature will compile identically. For performance and correctness questions, use the specific section relevant to the operation. This summary deliberately does not enumerate an unverified list of supported language features.

title: Native assets, minting and monetary policies
section: Native assets, minting and monetary policies
topics: Native assets, minting and monetary policies
text: Cardano supports native assets in its ledger. Minting and burning are governed by policies, and a policy identifier is derived from the policy script. Native assets do not require an ERC-20-style contract merely to be represented in the ledger. That does not mean anyone can mint arbitrary assets without satisfying a policy. Distinguish the ledger's native multi-asset support from a particular Plutus minting policy or off-chain SDK used to construct the transaction.
version_scope: See the cited source; no automatic version compatibility is assumed.
